text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Wave of reaction greets Cyprus's intention to buy the S-300 anti-aircraft system.
- President Clerides meets trade unions today to hammer out a deal on payment of cost of living allowance.
CYPRUS MAIL
- Cyprus rebuffs the United States on missile purchase.
- Missile purchase could mean war, warn diplomats.
- Drastic steps are to be taken to avert a water crisis.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Credit card sales rise sharply by 35 percent in 1996.
- Esso do a first with credit cards at local petrol stations.
HARAVGHI
- Missile purchase sparks reactions. "We have a right to buy them," says Communist Akel party chief Demetris Christofias.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- Nicosia refuses to budge on its plans to buy anti-aircraft missiles. US envoys are due in the region.
- Seismic activity in region increases.
- Reduction in borrowing rates is expected soon.
SIMERINI
- Cyprus and Greece refuse to succumb to threats and blackmail on the S-300 missile purchase.
- Extended drought is expected to have repercussions on the CPI.
